nodes.description: Preclinical only. Delivering a wild-type Tmc1 or Tmc2 coding sequence to hair cells with adeno-associated viral vectors restores sensory transduction, auditory brainstem responses and behavioural responses in Tmc1-mutant mice; later vectors recover inner and outer hair cell function, improve hair-cell survival and, in a humanized model carrying the equivalent of the human recessive p.N199I allele, bring ABR and DPOAE thresholds to wild-type levels across the frequency range. Three caveats carry over to any human application. The earliest and most complete rescues were in neonatal mice, a developmental stage corresponding to the human fetal inner ear, so the therapeutic window is the central translational problem - but it is not a closed one: the same vector partially recovered hearing in the recessive Baringo model with later-stage treatment, allele suppression worked in the mature Beethoven ear, and rescue has been reported in 2- to 8-week-old mice. Over-expression is not simply better: adding a WPRE element to boost Tmc1 expression gave inferior outcomes, which makes gene dosage an open design question. And a ClinicalTrials.gov search for TMC1 returned no registered studies, so no human efficacy or safety data exist. The allele-specific RNAi and Cas9-editing approaches in this literature target dominant DFNA36 alleles and do not apply to recessive loss of function.

nodes.description: Without a TMC1 pore, cochlear inner and outer hair cells generate no sound-evoked mechanoelectrical transduction current. Nothing compensates in the mature cochlea: Tmc2 is expressed only transiently in cochlear hair cells after birth, whereas Tmc1 expression persists, so the neonatal window in which TMC2 can carry transduction closes. Single deletion of Tmc1 in mouse abolishes hearing, and a humanized knock-in of a human recessive missense allele is deaf from birth for the same reason. Structurally normal hair bundles were reported for the Tmc1/Tmc2 double null rather than for the single null, and TMC proteins are in any case required for normal stereociliary bundle development, so this node claims loss of the current and not preservation of bundle architecture. The same TMC2 timing is the accepted explanation for the vestibular sparing of this disease, because vestibular hair cells keep expressing TMC2 into adulthood; that branch is discussed rather than modeled as a causal node, since persistence of TMC2 is not caused by the TMC1 lesion.

nodes.description: Hair cells that never transduce are progressively lost. The deafness (dn) mouse carrying a recessive Tmc1 exon deletion shows hair-cell degeneration, and longitudinal work on the same allele reports progressive hair-cell damage and loss after the failed maturation window. Because mammalian cochlear hair cells do not regenerate, this is the irreversible step of the disorder, and it is the node at which the entry conforms to the central effector of the sensorineural hair cell loss module. Two qualifications apply. First, the death pathway for recessive null genotypes is not established: the stereociliary PMCA2 / bundle-calcium / mitochondrial route was demonstrated for semidominant Tmc1 alleles whose hair cells still have MET current at P6, not for nulls. Second, hair-cell loss has never been examined in a person with DFNB7/11 and cannot be short of post-mortem histology, so the human form of this node is inferred from the mouse. Gene-replacement experiments showing enhanced hair-cell survival after restoring Tmc1 are the strongest evidence that the loss is a consequence of the gene lesion rather than an independent process.

nodes.description: Cochlear implantation is the standard intervention for the severe-to-profound loss that most DFNB7/11 genotypes produce. The biological rationale is favourable: the lesion is in the hair cell, so the spiral ganglion and auditory nerve - the structures an implant stimulates - are not the primary target of the disease. Reported outcomes are good. In an Italian series of three genotype-confirmed children, speech perception, nonverbal cognition and speech performance after implantation were comparable to children with DFNB1, and the authors explicitly did not reproduce the variable outcomes reported earlier in the literature. The Finnish cohort reports good speech perception in noise where diagnosis and rehabilitation were early. Both series are small and the inference that spiral ganglion integrity explains the result is from the biology of the lesion rather than from histology or electrophysiology in these patients.

nodes.description: Hair cells deprived of transduction current do not complete their postnatal functional maturation. In the deafness (dn) mouse, which carries a recessive Tmc1 deletion equivalent in class to the human truncating alleles, hair cells appear normal while immature and then fail to acquire the potassium currents that mark maturation, and the inner hair cell exocytotic machinery retains immature features into adulthood. Independent work manipulating the transduction apparatus shows the dependence runs through the MET current itself, and that it is also required to maintain the mature state, with adult cells reverting towards a pre-hearing phenotype when the current is removed. The mouse cochlea matures postnatally while the human cochlea is functional before birth, so the timing of this step does not transfer directly to human disease.

nodes.description: With no transduction current and a degenerating sensory epithelium, the cochlea produces no sound-evoked electrical output: compound action potentials and auditory brainstem responses are absent, and distortion-product otoacoustic emissions are absent because outer hair cells do not function. Notably, the failure of output precedes the loss of cells - homozygous mutants never show compound action potentials even at ages when many apical hair cells survive - so this node is driven by both the transduction and the degeneration arms of the chain. The afferent auditory pathway itself is not the primary lesion, which is the biological basis for expecting cochlear implants to work.

nodes.description: TMC1 is the pore-forming subunit of the mechanoelectrical transduction channel and localizes, with TMC2, to the tips of the shorter and middle rows of hair-cell stereocilia, where transduction occurs. Cysteine-mutagenesis mapping places four transmembrane domains, S4 to S7, in the channel pore, and reconstituted TMC1 carries mechanically gated ion channel activity on its own. When TMC1 is absent or non-functional the complex loses its permeation pathway; the residual scaffold of tip-link and auxiliary proteins - PCDH15, LHFPL5, TMIE and CIB2/CIB3 - remains without a conducting channel.

nodes.description: An alternative initiating lesion class. Some recessive TMC1 genotypes - the missense alleles p.Asn199Ile, p.Ser596Arg and p.Arg389Gln, and the donor-splice allele c.1404+1G>T that skips exon 16 and removes 60 amino acids - segregate with hearing loss that is less than profound. The same six-family series also includes a family homozygous for p.Arg34Ter, the nonsense founder allele that elsewhere accompanies profound loss, so this node is a class of outcome with a characteristic set of alleles rather than a genotype rule; allele class does not predict severity on its own. The authors' interpretation is hypo-functional rather than absent mechanotransduction channel activity, which places the lesion on the same axis as complete loss of function but short of it. This node exists separately because it has its own evidence and its own distinct clinical output, and because it is the part of the disease where residual hearing, and therefore amplification rather than implantation, becomes relevant. The residual-activity interpretation is an inference from the human audiometric severity plus the allele class; single-channel recordings have not been reported for these specific human alleles.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous pathogenic TMC1 variants abolish or reduce the function of transmembrane channel-like protein 1 in cochlear hair cells. The reported recessive allelic spectrum spans nonsense, frameshift, splice-site, copy-number, missense and in-frame classes. No published breakdown quantifies their relative shares for TMC1 specifically; in the one unselected hearing-loss cohort that reports variant classes across all recessive diagnoses, missense alleles were the largest single class, so this node does not claim that truncating alleles predominate. This is the initiating lesion of the disease and the node at which the disorder specializes the generic cochlear sensory-epithelium insult of the sensorineural hair cell loss module. The dominant DFNA36 alleles p.Asp572Asn and p.Met418Lys act by a different, channel-altering mechanism and are outside this entry.

evidence.reference_title: Prevalence and clinical features of autosomal dominant and recessive TMC1-associated hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: Most of the TMC1 variants are responsible for autosomal recessive hearing loss, with only 8 variants reported as causative for DFNA36.

evidence.reference_title: Identities, frequencies and origins of TMC1 mutations causing DFNB7/B11 deafness in Pakistan.
evidence.snippet: Overall, 9 different TMC1 mutations account for deafness in 19 (3.4%) of the 557 Pakistani families.

evidence.reference_title: Dominant and recessive deafness caused by mutations of a novel gene, TMC1, required for cochlear hair-cell function.
evidence.snippet: Tmc1 mRNA is expressed in hair cells of the postnatal mouse cochlea and vestibular end organs and is required for normal function of cochlear hair cells.

molecular_functions: mechanosensitive cation channel activity of the hair-cell MET channel

nodes.description: The double null abolishes all hair-cell mechanotransduction and adds profound vestibular dysfunction. It is the decisive experiment for the channel's identity and for TMC2 redundancy, but it over-models the human disease: people with biallelic TMC1 variants retain TMC2, so the vestibular arm of this phenotype is not part of DFNB7/11.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanotransduction in mouse inner ear hair cells requires transmembrane channel-like genes.
evidence.snippet: mice had profound vestibular dysfunction, deafness, and structurally normal hair cells that lacked all mechanotransduction activity

nodes.description: The engineered null. Homozygotes are deaf, while vestibular function is preserved because vestibular hair cells continue to express TMC2. This model is the basis of the vestibular-sparing explanation for the human disease and is the recipient for most of the gene-replacement work. No claim is made here about hair-bundle architecture: the "structurally normal hair cells" observation in PMID:22105175 is reported for the Tmc1/Tmc2 double null, and PMID:29872055 finds TMC proteins required for normal stereociliary bundle development.

evidence.reference_title: Mechanotransduction in mouse inner ear hair cells requires transmembrane channel-like genes.
evidence.snippet: Tmc2 expression was transient in early postnatal mouse cochlear hair cells but persisted in vestibular hair cells.

nodes.description: A comparative model showing that subunit requirements are not conserved: zebrafish hearing does not require Tmc1 specifically, and only the triple mutant is deaf. It is useful for channel biology and as a caution against reading subunit requirements across species, and it is not a model of the human disease.
nodes.id: Zebrafish tmc1, tmc2a and tmc2b mutants

evidence.reference_title: Tmc proteins are essential for zebrafish hearing where Tmc1 is not obligatory.
evidence.snippet: Hearing however is absent in triple-mutant zebrafish that lack Tmc1, Tmc2a and Tmc2b.

nodes.description: The most recurrent recessive TMC1 allele. A founder allele in Pakistan, where it causes deafness in 1.8% of 557 families, and in Saudi Arabia, where 8 of 12 TMC1 families share it with linkage disequilibrium across flanking SNPs. It was also detected among African-American and northern European control samples, which the authors read as evidence that TMC1 alleles contribute to the genetic load of deafness beyond the populations where they were first mapped.

evidence.reference_title: Identities, frequencies and origins of TMC1 mutations causing DFNB7/B11 deafness in Pakistan.
evidence.snippet: Genotype analysis of p.R34X-linked markers indicates that it arose from a common founder.

evidence.reference_title: Identities, frequencies and origins of TMC1 mutations causing DFNB7/B11 deafness in Pakistan.
evidence.snippet: We also detected p.R34X among normal control samples of African-American and northern European origins, raising the possibility that p.R34X and other mutations of TMC1 are prevalent contributors to the genetic load of deafness across a variety of populations and continents.

evidence.reference_title: Identification of TMC1 as a relatively common cause for nonsyndromic hearing loss in the Saudi population.
evidence.snippet: Eight families in our cohort were found to share the pathogenic p.Arg34Ter mutation and linkage disequilibrium was observed between p.Arg34Ter and SNPs investigated.

nodes.description: Recurrent nonsense allele reported in Turkish families and, in the deep-research literature survey, in Sudanese families. It is one of the two previously known alleles recovered in the Turkish mutation-analysis series.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation analysis of TMC1 identifies four new mutations and suggests an additional deafness gene at loci DFNA36 and DFNB7/11.
evidence.snippet: The pathogenic variants we found included two known mutations, c.100C>T and c.1165C>T, and four new mutations, c.2350C>T, c.776+1G>A, c.767delT and c.1166G>A.

evidence.reference_title: Novel TMC1 structural and splice variants associated with congenital nonsyndromic deafness in a Sudanese pedigree.
evidence.snippet: The c.1165C>T ... mutation was also observed in four out of 243 unrelated deaf Sudanese individuals, but none of the mutations was found among 292 normal hearing controls.

nodes.description: Donor splice-site transversion found homozygous in families with moderate-to-severe loss. Patient cDNA shows skipping of exon 16 and loss of 60 amino acids, making this a measured in-frame hypomorphic allele rather than a predicted one, and it is the clearest molecular anchor for the hypomorphic branch of the pathograph.

evidence.reference_title: Recessive mutations of TMC1 associated with moderate to severe hearing loss.
evidence.snippet: TMC1 cDNA sequence from affected subjects homozygous for the donor splice site transversion c.1404 + 1G > T revealed skipping of exon 16, deleting 60 amino acids from the TMC1 protein.

nodes.description: Nonsense allele enriched in the Finnish population and interpreted as a founder variant there. It appears in recessive genotypes with congenital moderate-to-profound hearing loss in the Finnish cohort.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Characteristics of Finnish Patients with Autosomal Recessive and Dominant Non-Syndromic Hearing Loss Due to Pathogenic TMC1 Variants.
evidence.snippet: We show that the TMC1 c.1534C>T, p.(Arg512*) variant is likely a founder variant that is enriched in the Finnish population.

nodes.description: Missense allele recurrent in the Xiamen area of south-eastern China, homozygous in the probands of three families and found in compound heterozygotes with four other TMC1 alleles in a school-based series. Haplotype analysis across 53 SNPs found the homozygous probands' haplotypes identical, which is the basis for a local founder effect.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation spectra and founder effect of TMC1 in patients with non-syndromic deafness in Xiamen area, China.
evidence.snippet: The probands of three families were found to be homozygous for TMC1 c.2050G>C, and their parents were all heterozygous for the TMC1 c.2050G>C mutation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation spectra and founder effect of TMC1 in patients with non-syndromic deafness in Xiamen area, China.
evidence.snippet: The haplotypes of the probands of families with TMC1 c.2050G>C were identical.

evidence.reference_title: [Analysis of TMC1 gene variants and prenatal diagnosis in four Chinese families affected with deafness].
evidence.snippet: and homozygosity of c.2050G>C (p.D684H) in family 4

nodes.description: The spontaneous recessive allele that led to the gene. It is the closest available model of the human truncating genotypes: homozygotes lack auditory responses, their hair cells look normal while immature and then fail to acquire the maturation potassium currents, and hair cells degenerate progressively. Because it is a spontaneous deletion rather than an engineered human variant, it models the allele class and not any particular human variant.

evidence.reference_title: Tmc1 is necessary for normal functional maturation and survival of inner and outer hair cells in the mouse cochlea.
evidence.snippet: The deafness (dn) and Beethoven (Bth) mutant mice are models for profound congenital deafness (DFNB7/B11) and progressive hearing loss (DFNA36), respectively
